answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a refundable stake bond: before an identity may trade, it locks tokens that peers can slash if duplicate or fake identities are proven. Like juniper roots anchoring one plant firmly, one bond anchors one identity, so spawning thousands of fakes becomes expensive instead of free. Honest agents earn the bond back plus a saffron-grade reputation premium over time, while a detected sybil forfeits its stake, so attacker cost scales with every fake while honest participation stays cheap, like composing one sonnet rather than forging a library.
